newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SE Asian buyers out due to volatile Chicago market.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian buyers out due to volatile Chicago market.

text.p: Southeast Asian grains and oilseeds buyers sat on the sidelines to wait for the dust to settle over a volatile Chicago futures market, regional traders said on Thursday.
With most countries around the region having ample coverage, there was no incentive for most to pick up material for July onwards shipment, they said.
"It's pretty quiet on the meal and corn side," a dealer for a U.S. commodity house in Singapore said. "The volatility in Chicago has a lot to do with it. It certainly has got people skittish."
Futures prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) climbed over the past few weeks until a bearish U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) crop report on Monday knocked the market back.
Soybean, corn and soy product prices in the CBOT slid overnight with the July soybean futures contract diving 10-1/2 U.S. cents down at US$8.64 a bushel.

"People feel prices still have some room to come off. Combined with pretty good coverage and the fact that the trend in most commodities is down, people are in no hurry to buy," another dealer for a commodity company in Singapore said.
Most of the trade is waiting for some open positions on meal to come up within the next few weeks.
Dealers believe Indonesia may need up to 50,000 tonnes of meal while Thailand may be in the market for 20,000-30,000 tonnes of meal.
Malaysia will probably stay out for the meantime because it has bought ample supplies of meal, they said.
"I think buyers there have to come in and fill those positions soon. But it won't be this week because they're in no hurry to do so," a trader said.
Another dealer estimated that buyers from Indonesia and Thailand will probably "need to step up in the next two weeks".
Traders said the likely source of the meal would probably be a South American country like Argentine, whose meal still enjoys a discount to U.S. origin.

Argentine meal coming into Southeast Asia was seen by the trade at around $324-$326 a tonne C&F for June/July shipment on a Handy while U.S. meal was quoted at $357-$359 a tonne C&F on a Panamax for the same shipment period.
A corn glut in Malaysia and ample stocks in Indonesia and Thailand will preclude any buying for corn in the region.
"It's really been quiet. We've not heard anything being done lately," a trader for a European commodity house said.

U.S. corn was slowly becoming competitive again, dealers said. It was quoted by the trade at $143-$145 a tonne C&F for June/July shipment on a Panamax while Chinese corn was seen a shade lower at $143-$144 a tonne C&F on the same basis.
